headline: "FED RATE FEARS" HAMMER SILVER AGAIN — Down for Second Straight Session as Rate-Hike Odds Resurface
snippet: Silver continued its retreat on May 18 as investors repriced Federal Reserve rate-hike odds following April's hotter-than-expected 3.8% CPI print. The metal has been violently volatile this month — briefly spiking toward $87 after the US-China tariff truce before reversing sharply on inflation data.

headline: UBS SLASHES Silver Deficit Forecast 80% — Structural Bull Case Collapses from 300M oz to 60M oz
snippet: UBS analysts Wayne Gordon and Dominic Schnider cut their 2026 global silver supply deficit estimate from ~300 million ounces to just 60–70 million ounces, citing weaker photovoltaic and jewellery demand plus mine output approaching 850M oz. The bank also lowered its end-Q2 silver price target from $100 to $85/oz.

headline: GOLD FALLS on 3.8% CPI — The Counterintuitive Mechanism Nobody Explains
snippet: Gold has corrected 16% from its January all-time high of $5,589/oz even as US inflation hit 3.8% — the highest since May 2023. The analysis explains the mechanism: hot CPI repriced Fed expectations from two cuts to zero, strengthening the dollar and mechanically pressuring the metal despite inflation theoretically supporting it.

headline: 20.7 g/t GOLD OVER 11 METRES — Galway Metals Extends Clarence Stream High-Grade Zone, Q2 Resource Update Looms
snippet: Galway Metals (TSXV: GWM) released assay results from seven drill holes at its Southwest Deposit within the Clarence Stream project in New Brunswick, returning 20.7 g/t gold over 11.0 metres from the GMZ and Adrian Zones. An updated mineral resource estimate for the project — currently 922,000 indicated oz at 2.3 g/t — is expected before end of Q2 2026.

headline: ONYX GOLD Drills 99.5m at 1.2 g/t with NEW 4.9 g/t High-Grade Structure at Munro-Croesus
snippet: Onyx Gold (TSXV: ONYX) reported a new high-grade structure at Argus Main within its fully-funded 110,000m drill program at the Munro-Croesus project in Ontario, returning 4.9 g/t gold over 15.0m inside a broader 1.3 g/t zone spanning 77.2m. A companion hole intersected 99.5m at 1.2 g/t, expanding the Argus System footprint 75 km east of Timmins.

headline: CABRAL DOUBLES to 6 Drill Rigs, Hits 62.5 g/t Bonanza Intercept at Jerimum Cima Target, Brazil
snippet: Cabral Gold (TSXV: CBR) intersected 10.2m at 8.7 g/t gold including a bonanza-grade 1.3m at 62.5 g/t at the Jerimum Cima target in Brazil's Cuiú Cuiú gold district, while simultaneously doubling its fleet to six drill rigs at the MG deposit. The company targets commercial gold production from its Phase 1 heap-leach operation in Q4 2026.

headline: COPPER RETREATS from $13,400/t Record — Chinese Buyers Hold Back, 2026 Surplus Forecast Widened to 300kt
snippet: Copper futures retreated from record highs near $6.50/lb (~$13,400/t) as Chinese buyers delayed purchases at elevated prices and US inflation data reinforced rate-hike bets. Analysts widened their 2026 surplus forecast to 300,000 tonnes from a prior 160,000 tonnes estimate, though AI infrastructure and grid build-out continue to support the long-term structural thesis.

headline: MP MATERIALS Q1 2026: Magnetics Revenue UP 306%, NdPr Output at Record — Magnet Sales Set for H2
snippet: MP Materials (NYSE: MP) reported Q1 2026 revenue of $90.65M (+49% YoY), with its magnetics division surging 306% to $21M as the company ramps toward domestic magnet sales in H2 2026. NdPr oxide production hit a record 917 metric tons — up 63% year-over-year — with GM qualification of magnets currently underway.

headline: J.P. MORGAN, ING HOLD $5,000 Gold Target — Why Institutional Desks Ignore the 16% Correction
snippet: Despite gold's 16% correction from its January ATH of $5,589, J.P. Morgan forecasts a Q4 2026 average of $5,055 while ING targets $5,000 by year-end. The bull case rests on 244 tonnes of central bank buying in Q1 2026 alone — beating the five-year average — and bar-and-coin demand at its second-highest quarterly level ever.

headline: GOLD MINERS LAG the Metal — Record Margins at Sub-$2,000 AISC Signal a Valuation Re-Rating Is Due
snippet: Gold producers are trading at a 10% discount to historical EV/EBITDA multiples even as industry-wide all-in sustaining costs hold below $2,000/oz, generating record margins at current prices. Analysts argue operational leverage, accelerating M&A, and continued underallocation make mining equities the better-value play over physical gold through the rest of 2026.

headline: LITHIUM REBOUNDS to $15,000–$17,000/t — Battery Storage Boom Reshapes Demand Outlook After 85% Slump
snippet: Lithium carbonate prices have recovered to the $15,000–$17,000/t range after an 85% collapse from late-2022 highs, driven by accelerating grid-scale energy storage system demand and China's cut to VAT export rebates on lithium-ion batteries. Oversupply persists but the demand trajectory has shifted, with ESS demand seen as the structural catalyst for a sustained recovery.

headline: U.S. MILESTONE: Energy Fuels Qualifies Domestic Heavy REE Oxide for Permanent Magnets Ahead of China Ban
snippet: Energy Fuels (NYSE: UUUU) announced its US-produced heavy rare earth oxide has been successfully qualified for use in permanent magnets — a first for domestic production — ahead of a January 1, 2027 ban on Chinese-origin NdFeB magnets in US defense systems. The company also reported Q1 2026 uranium revenue of $35.7M and $956M in working capital, underpinned by its uranium operations.
